title: Max and the Turkey Trot
author: Shellfie original
credit: An original story written for the McKinley Bulldogs.

pages: Every November, McKinley has the Turkey Trot. It is a fun run, and every class gets a turn to race around the field.
Max has been practicing all week. Max runs to the mailbox and back. Max runs around the kitchen table. Grandma says, "Please practice outside!"
On the big day, parent helpers hand out stickers and cheer. Some grown-ups wear turkey hats with floppy red parts that wiggle when they jump.
Max's class lines up at the start. The coach blows the whistle. Tweet! Everyone runs.
Max runs fast at first. Too fast! Halfway around, Max's legs feel like noodles.
Then Max hears Lupe cheering from the side. "Go, Max! You can do it!" Max keeps going, one step at a time.
Max does not finish first. Max does not finish last. But Max finishes, and that is what counts.
At the end, everyone gets a sticker. Max high-fives the coach and helps cheer for the next class.
That night, Max says, "The Turkey Trot is not about winning. It is about running together." Then Max falls asleep at the dinner table.
